simple.meaning: שִׁדָּה (shiddâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a wife (as mistress of the house).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Ecclesiastes, beginning at Ecclesiastes 2:8. Its contexts include family line, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שִׁדָּה (H7705).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שִׁדָּה (shiddâh) / H7705 is traced through Ecclesiastes 2:8 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H7705. shiddah שִׁדָּה noun feminine meaning unknown; — only singular and plural וְשִׁדּוֺת שִׁדָּה Eccl 2:8 , apparently appositive of תַּעֲנגֻוֺת ( ᵐ5 οἰνοχόον καὶ οἰνοχόας , i.e. וְשֹׁדוֺת שֹׁדֶה , from Aramaic שְׁדָא pour out [but not spec. of wine]; Aq κυλίκιον καὶ κυλίκια (compare ᵑ9 ), probably from same √; Dl Prol. 97 Kö ii. 1. 161 Wild Siegf compare Assyrian šadâdu , love (Siegf 'Haremsperlen'), but this word lacks evidence; possibly וְשָׁרוֺת שָׂרָה , see I. שָׂרָה
